name: Elton Shouts for Bob to Get Off the Ledge
description: Elton sees Bob on the window ledge and immediately leans out, shouting for him to get down. He calls out Bob's name and tells him to get his butt off the ledge, urging him to come away right away.
related_events: Elton yells at Bob to leave the window ledge

name: Elton Applauds Through the Windshield
description: Elton is seen through the windshield, clapping his hands in applause.
related_events: Elton applauds from behind the windshield

name: Bobby Arrives at the Bungalow
description: The car comes to a stop in front of a small bungalow on a low-rent residential street. Bobby opens the door, steps out, and walks along the path leading to the house. He reaches the door, opens it, and goes inside.
related_events: Bobby exits the car and enters the bungalow

name: Start the Car and Drive Off
description: He turns the key, the engine roars to life. With a sharp jerk, he slams the gearshift into place and grips the steering wheel tightly.
related_events: Character starts car motor and shifts into gear angrily

name: Traveling North on the Pacific Coast Highway
description: The character drives north along the Pacific Coast Highway. The car moves steadily, following the coastline under open sky.
related_events: Car travels north along Pacific Coast Highway

name: Bobby Drives Through the Oil Field at Night
description: Bobby, still wearing his hard hat, drives through an oil field after dark. The derricks stand silhouetted against the night sky, their work lights glowing brightly as they continue operating. The road stretches ahead, lined with machinery and the hum of distant activity, as he moves steadily through the illuminated industrial landscape.
related_events: Bobby drives through the oil field at night

name: Cars Surround Bobby's Vehicle on the Road
description: Other cars move in close, positioning themselves in front of, behind, and on both sides of Bobby's car. The vehicles lock into place, leaving no space for Bobby to move. The road becomes a tight enclosure, with metal and glass pressing in from every direction.
related_events: Cars surround Bobby's vehicle on all sides

name: Bobby Navigates Freeway Traffic
description: Bobby's car slows as it moves into a jammed freeway. The traffic is heavy, and the vehicle reduces speed, matching the flow of the surrounding cars.
related_events: Bobby's car slows due to freeway traffic congestion

name: Bobby Starts Playing as Traffic Moves
description: Bobby begins to play just as the traffic starts moving. A truck nearby begins to roll forward, and around the same time, Bobby starts playing, matching his actions to the motion unfolding on the road.
related_events: Bobby begins playing as traffic starts moving

name: Truck Begins Right Lane Change
description: The truck's right-turn indicator flashes as it starts to move across the lanes, shifting position within the flow of traffic.
related_events: Truck starts moving across lanes with right-turn indicator flashing

name: Bobby Slams Car Into Park and Storms Out
description: He suddenly throws the car into park, yanks the door open, and steps out without another word.
related_events: Bobby expresses frustration and exits the vehicle

name: Bobby Smiles, Rayette Caresses His Neck
description: Bobby looks over at Rayette and smiles. She returns his gaze and reaches over, gently caressing the back of his neck.
related_events: Bobby smiles at Rayette
Rayette caresses the back of Bobby's neck

name: Bobby Arrives at Rayette's House
description: Bobby steps out of his car and walks up the path toward Rayette's house. He reaches the door and goes inside.
related_events: Bobby exits his car and walks to Rayette's house
Bobby enters Rayette's house

name: Bobby and Elton Turned Away from Rig
description: Bobby and Elton, unsteady on their feet after a night of drinking, made their way toward a derrick and began climbing the stairs to the rig floor. As they ascended, the driller intercepted them, took in their condition, and blocked them from continuing. He informed them they were not fit to work and sent them away for the day.
related_events: Bobby and Elton attempt to climb to the rig floor after a night of drinking
Driller stops Bobby and Elton from working due to intoxication

name: Bobby Wins the Lunch Break Poker Game
description: During a lunch break, Bobby lays down a strong poker hand at a makeshift table. He sweeps a pile of crumpled bills and loose change toward himself as the other players, including Elton and three toolpushers, watch. Around them, workers in the background move about, some pulling on clean shirts after their shifts.
related_events: Bobby plays winning poker hand and collects winnings
related_occasions: Impromptu Card Game During Lunch Break

name: Bobby Pulls Out the Bench and Plays a Chopin Prelude
description: Bobby pulled the bench out from beneath the piano, sat down, and began playing a Chopin prelude.
related_events: Bobby pulls bench out from beneath the piano
Bobby begins playing a Chopin prelude

name: Bobby Loads Suitcase and Drives Away
description: Bobby throws a suitcase through the rear window of his car, walks around to the driver's side, opens the door, and gets inside.
related_events: Bobby places suitcase in car through rear window
Bobby enters driver's side of car

name: Bobby Finds a Piano in the Truck
description: As Bobby steps out of the truck, he notices a padded protector on the floor. He reaches down, pulls it off, and reveals an upright piano underneath. He crouches beside it, places his fingers on the keys, and plays a few notes.
related_events: Bobby discovers an upright piano under a padded protector
Bobby plays a few notes on the upright piano

name: Bobby Stops the Music and Asks Ray to Leave
description: Bobby's hand slashes at the arm of the record player, pulling it across the grooves and cutting off Tammy Wynette's voice. The room falls silent. He turns and looks at Ray. 'Do you want to go with me, Ray?'
related_events: Bobby stops the record player abruptly
Bobby asks Ray to accompany him

name: Bobby Exits the Truck and Wanders the Sidewalk
description: The truck slows and stops at a traffic signal. Bobby opens the door and steps out, moving onto the sidewalk. He begins to walk along the city streets, unsteady and without direction, drifting past dimly lit storefronts and empty lots under the glow of scattered streetlights.
related_events: Truck comes to a stop at a signal
Bobby exits the truck and moves to the sidewalk
Bobby wanders aimlessly along city streets

name: Bobby Finds and Enters Studio A
description: Bobby walks through a series of hallways, glancing at door numbers as he passes. He stops in front of a door marked Studio A, pauses for a moment, then turns the handle, opens the door, and steps inside.
related_events: Bobby checks door numbers while moving through hallways
Bobby hesitates before entering Studio A
Bobby opens the door to Studio A and steps inside

name: Elton and Betty Sing a Nursery Rhyme
description: Elton sits with Betty on his knee, bouncing her gently as they sing 'Ride a Cockhorse To Banbury Cross' together. Betty throws her head back, laughing with unrestrained delight. Elton grins, caught up in the moment, and turns to Bobby, who sits on the couch with an arm around Twinky and a beer in hand. 'God, id'n she the cutest damn thing in your life!' Elton exclaims, his voice full of warmth.
related_events: Elton rides Betty on his leg while singing a nursery rhyme
Betty laughs with childlike hysteria during the singing
Elton looks at Bobby and exclaims about Betty's charm

name: Elton Tries to Follow Bobby onto the Off Ramp
description: Elton steered his vehicle toward the off ramp as Bobby's truck pulled ahead. He leaned on the horn and waved his arm out the window, trying to push through the lanes. Cars to his right moved closer together, leaving no space to merge, and the gap closed just as he approached the exit.
related_events: Elton attempts to follow Bobby's truck onto an off ramp
Elton honks horn and signals with arm while crossing lanes
Traffic blocks Elton from crossing to the off ramp

name: Twinky's Intimate Outburst with Bobby
description: Twinky opens her mouth and lets out a piercing wail, her face glistening with moisture as it contorts through expressions of deep distress. The sound shifts abruptly into a sharp, ecstatic screech, delivered with practiced intensity. She reaches up, pulls Bobby down onto her, and presses close, whispering 'Donnie, oh Donnie...' into his ear.
related_events: Twinky emits a keening wail expressing anguish
Twinky delivers an ecstatic screech and pulls Bobby down onto her
Twinky whispers Donnie's name into Bobby's ear

name: Elton and Bobby Work the Rig Under Supervision
description: Elton and Bobby work on the drilling rig as part of a four-man crew. The Driller stands nearby, calling out instructions for each step of the operation. Bobby fumbles with his tasks, moving cautiously and pausing to check his actions, while Elton handles his duties with steady precision. Throughout the shift, the Derrickman leans against a railing in the background, arms crossed, watching but not engaging in the work.
related_events: Elton and Bobby operate drilling rig as part of four-man team
Driller issues operational directives to rig team
Bobby demonstrates inexperience in rig operations
Derrickman remains idle in background during rig operations

name: Bobby Investigates Traffic Jam on Freeway
description: Bobby exits his car and walks along the freeway. He steps up onto the fender of a nearby vehicle to look ahead, trying to see what is causing the traffic backup. The driver of the car shouts at him to get off.
related_events: Bobby moves down the freeway away from his car
Bobby steps up onto the fender of a nearby car to investigate traffic jam
Driver shouts at Bobby to get off the car

name: Elton Takes the Driver's Seat
description: Bobby steps out of the car and moves down the freeway, leaving the vehicle behind. Elton shifts across the seat and takes the driver's position. As Bobby walks away, he climbs onto the fender of another car to look ahead, and a driver shouts at him to get off.
related_events: Elton slides into the driver's seat of the car

name: Bobby Arrives and Is Served Coffee
description: Bobby enters the diner and takes a seat at the counter. Another waitress approaches with a coffee Silex, gestures toward him, and he nods. She pours him a cup of coffee.
related_events: Bobby enters the diner and takes a seat at the counter
Another waitress offers coffee to Bobby using a Silex and pours him a cup

name: Rayette Clears Tables and Avoids Bobby
description: Rayette clears plates from an empty table and moves across the diner. She approaches the only other customer, totals his bill, and collects payment. Another waitress brings a coffee Silex and offers Bobby a cup; he nods, and she pours. Rayette walks to the register, deposits several bills, then turns and exits through the kitchen door.
related_events: Rayette clears plates from an empty table
Rayette totals the bill for the only other customer
Rayette continues working while ignoring Bobby
Rayette deposits bills into the register and exits to the kitchen

name: Bobby climbs onto the truck and looks over the traffic
description: Bobby cuts in front of another car and climbs into the rear of a truck. He moves forward to the front of the truck and looks out over the cab. From there, he sees the congestion of cars in all four lanes. Elton calls out to him, telling him to stop fooling around.
related_events: Bobby cuts in front of another car and climbs into the rear of the truck
Bobby moves to the front of the truck and looks out over the cab

name: Elton Calls Out to Bobby on the Truck
description: From off-screen, Elton shouts to Bobby, telling him to stop fooling around. Bobby is on the truck, having climbed into the rear and moved toward the front, where he looks out over the cab. Cars are backed up in all four lanes around them.
related_events: Elton calls out to Bobby to stop fooling around

name: Rayette Sings a Ballad While Bobby Listens
description: Rayette sings a song, her voice steady and expressive, using words about fire and trails to describe love that endures through hardship. She sings of small fires and big fires, of heartache and longing, and of someone returning in the end. Bobby laughs at something in her delivery, then tells her he loves it. She continues singing, describing the paths someone might take, when Bobby suddenly interrupts, his attention caught by something ahead on the road. Rayette stops mid-lyric, following his gaze.
related_events: Rayette sings a song about enduring love and emotional fire
Bobby laughs in response to Rayette's singing
Bobby expresses admiration for Rayette's song
Rayette sings lyrics about blazing trails and emotional connection

name: Bobby Sees the Overturned Car
description: Bobby stops listening to Rayette’s song and stares at something ahead on the highway. He frowns and mutters, “What the hell is that?” Rayette follows his gaze and sees an overturned car on the left side of the road, with two people standing near it, arguing.
related_events: Bobby becomes distracted by something on the road ahead
Bobby reacts with confusion to something ahead on the road
Rayette identifies a potential accident on the highway

name: Mother Teaches Bobby the Piano Etude
description: Bobby sits on the piano bench beside his mother, his feet swinging slightly as she plays the etude slowly and carefully. He watches her hands, then turns his face toward her arm, leaning into her as he places his thumb in his mouth. She continues playing, her hand gently resting on his back between phrases, guiding the music with quiet patience.
related_events: Mother demonstrates piano etude for Bobby
Bobby leans against mother while sucking thumb

name: The Family Plays Chamber Music
description: Bobby's father, along with his two brothers and his sister, performs a chamber music piece in the room. The music fills the space with a steady, measured rhythm. Bobby sits in a chair nearby, his feet swinging gently in time with the beat. The sound surrounds him as his mother joins him on the piano bench, demonstrating the etude he is learning. He leans against her arm, thumb in his mouth, listening as the family's playing continues in the background.
related_events: Father and siblings perform chamber music piece

name: Carl and Tita Play Piano Duet
description: Carl and Tita, now teenagers, sit side by side on the piano bench and play a four-hands piece at an andante rhythm. Their performance is precise and technically masterful, the music filling the room with a controlled, measured flow.
related_events: Carl and Tita perform four-hands piano piece at andante rhythm

name: Bobby Confronts Rayette at the Diner
description: Bobby stands by a pickup truck next to Rayette's car. When she exits the diner and sees him, she hesitates, then walks past him toward her car. He speaks to her, saying he was with Elton the previous night. As she reaches for her car door, he steps behind her and closes it before she can get in. Gently taking hold of her arm, he turns her toward him and brings his face close to hers. As she turns her head away, he begins to kiss her neck. She looks down at the ground and quietly says, 'You son of a bitch.'
related_events: Bobby confronts Rayette outside the diner
Bobby blocks Rayette from entering her car

name: Bobby Forces a Kiss on Rayette
description: Bobby reaches behind Rayette and pushes her car door shut. He takes hold of her arm, turns her toward him, and brings his face close to hers. As she turns away, he begins to kiss her neck. She lowers her gaze to the ground and quietly says, 'You son of a bitch.'
related_events: Bobby grabs Rayette's arm and turns her toward him
Bobby kisses Rayette's neck against her resistance

name: Bobby Kisses Rayette's Neck, She Rebukes Him
description: Bobby moves behind Rayette and gently takes hold of her arm, turning her toward him. He brings his face close to hers and begins to kiss her neck as she turns away. Rayette lowers her gaze to the ground and quietly says, 'You son of a bitch.'
related_events: Rayette verbally rebukes Bobby

name: Bobby Operates Backhoe to Excavate and Load Earth
description: The toothed bucket of a backhoe digs into the earth and lifts a load of soil into the air. Bobby, wearing a hard-hat and heavy gloves, operates the controls from the cab. The backhoe swings sideways and empties the soil into the bed of a waiting truck. Nearby, Elton and other crew members move about the site as part of the work team, handling pipes, welding tubing, and climbing the derrick structure. During breaks, they gather near a beer wagon, exchanging jokes and banter.
related_events: Backhoe operator excavates earth at construction site
Crew deposits earth into truck bed

name: Bobby and Elton Work the Derrick Crew at Signal Hill
description: Bobby and Elton, wearing hard hats and heavy gloves, work alongside a team of tool-pusher operators on the oil derricks of Signal Hill. They handle pull rods, make and break joints on the rig floor, weld sections of tubing, and carry pipes across the worksite. Both men climb the steel framework of the rig, moving through the structure as they perform their tasks. During breaks, they exchange jokes and banter with the crew near the beer wagon. The backhoe digs into the earth, lifts a load of soil, and swings it into the bed of a waiting truck, while Bobby operates the machinery with practiced ease.
related_events: Bobby and Elton work on derrick crew at Signal Hill

name: Bobby and Elton Play the Dozens on Beer Break
description: Bobby and Elton sit on the edge of the derrick floor during a break, cracking open beers. Around them, the crew gathers, leaning on toolboxes and pipes. Laughter rises as one worker hurls a sharp joke at another, who fires back with a louder, more exaggerated insult. Bobby smirks, takes a swig, and delivers a taunt that draws hoots and jeers. Elton claps back with a grin, launching into a string of playful jabs. The men laugh, shout, and nudge each other, the rhythm of their banter rolling like a game, until a whistle blows and they toss their cans, returning to the rigs.
related_events: Workers engage in verbal banter during beer break

name: Bobby Gets Ready for the Family Recital
description: Bobby, ten years old and wearing a formal suit, sits still as his mother combs his hair with careful attention. The house is quiet except for the rustle of fabric and the soft strokes of the comb. A program lies nearby, listing the evening's performances: Bach, Handel, Mozart, Beethoven, and finally, Grebner—Five Easy Pieces, to be played by Robert Dupea.
related_events: Bobby prepares for family recital while his mother combs his hair

name: The Dupea Family Recital
description: Nicholas and Carl Dupea took the stage first, playing a sonata in C major for two violins by Bach. Isabelle Dupea followed, singing 'Like As a Lovelorn Turtle' by Hendel. Elizabeth Dupea performed next, playing Mozart's Rondo Alla Turca on the piano. Herbart Dupea then played Beethoven's Piano Sonata, Opus 110. The recital concluded with Robert Dupea performing Grebner's Five Easy Pieces.
related_events: Nicholas and Carl Dupea perform Bach sonata
Isabelle Dupea sings Hendel's lovelorn turtle piece
Elizabeth Dupea performs Mozart's Rondo Alla Turca
Herbart Dupea performs Beethoven's Piano Sonata Opus 110
Robert Dupea performs Five Easy Pieces by Grebner

name: Bobby's Outburst in Traffic
description: Bobby gestures angrily at the traffic, his face tight with irritation. He takes a swig from a half pint of hard liquor, then slams his hand against the steering wheel. 'Can you believe this shit?' he shouts. Ahead, a truck carries furniture covered in padded wraps. Elton, finishing a tune on his ukulele, says, 'Give 'em the horn, Bob.' Bobby glares at the cars ahead. 'Look at these assholes! What the hell are they doing?!'
related_events: Bobby expresses frustration about traffic conditions
Bobby drinks from a half pint of hard liquor
Bobby strikes the steering wheel in anger
Bobby verbally confronts other drivers in traffic
Elton suggests honking the horn at other drivers

name: Bobby and Elton Notice Furniture Truck in Traffic
description: Through the windshield, a truck carrying several pieces of furniture covered in padded wraps moves slowly ahead, visible a few cars away. Bobby glares at it, still gripping the steering wheel, while Elton watches from the passenger seat.
related_events: Observation of a furniture-laden truck ahead in traffic

name: Elton Finishes Ukulele Song in the Car
description: Elton strums the final notes of a song on his ukulele while sitting in the car. The music fades out, and Bobby, holding a half pint of cheap liquor, looks out at the traffic. He takes a drink, then slams the steering wheel. Ahead, a truck carries furniture covered in padded wraps. Elton leans forward and says, 'Give 'em the horn, Bob.' Bobby shouts, 'Look at these assholes! What the hell are they doing?!'
related_events: Elton finishes performing a song on the ukulele

name: Family at the Funeral Pew
description: The camera moves along the family seated on the pew as mourners walk slowly past the open casket of Isabelle Dupea. The pale profile of her face rests in the satin lining. Nicholas, Tita, Carl, and Herbert rise and step into the aisle, following the line toward the casket. Bobby stands from his seat and moves toward the aisle, but instead of approaching the casket, he turns and walks up the chapel, exiting through the doors.
related_events: Camera pans across family members on pew
Bobby avoids looking at his mother's body
Procession of mourners moves past open casket

name: Nicholas Leads Family to the Casket
description: After the last of the family friends passes by the casket, Nicholas rises from his seat and steps into the aisle. He walks forward, followed by Tita, Carl, and Herbert, moving slowly toward the open casket where Isabelle Dupea lies. One by one, they approach the casket as part of the funeral service. Bobby, seated on the family pew, stands and moves toward the aisle but stops briefly, then turns and walks out of the chapel without approaching.
related_events: Nicholas and others move toward the casket after family friends pay respects

name: Bobby Leaves the Chapel During the Funeral
description: Bobby rises from his seat on the family pew and walks toward the aisle. He pauses briefly, standing still as the others move toward the casket. Then he turns and walks up the aisle, passing the rows of pews, and exits through the chapel doors.
related_events: Bobby hesitates in the aisle then leaves the chapel

name: Elton Recalls His Time as a Derrickman
description: Elton sits on the couch with Bobby and Stoney, all facing the TV. He shakes his head and says he swore he’d never return to oil field work, wondering how he let himself be talked into it. He tells Bobby he used to be a derrickman in the southern fields and hated it. He recalls working 90 feet up on a derrick tour, suspended by a harness like a circus performer, nearly breaking his neck. He brings up Stoney’s brother, asking if he wasn’t a well-puller, the one with three fingers. Stoney, keeping her eyes on the screen, confirms it was her brother Cruser.
related_events: Elton expresses regret about returning to oil field work
Elton recounts experience as derrickman in southern oil fields
Elton recalls working 90 feet up on a derrick tour
Elton mentions Stoney's brother being a well-puller with three fingers
Stoney confirms identity of her brother Cruser

name: Rayette Cooing Over Infant, Elton Teases Bobby
description: Rayette sits on a chair adjacent to the couch, holding an infant in her lap. She coos over the baby, gazing at it and murmuring about how cute it is. Without looking away, she reaches over to Bobby and asks for a swig of his beer. He hands it to her, and she takes a sip before returning it. Elton, seated on the couch with Bobby and Stoney, watches the TV and recalls working as a derrickman, then turns to Bobby with a gap-toothed smile. He jokes that Bobby should get a child of his own. Bobby stands up, stretches his arms, and replies with a dry remark about living in a trailer park with his front teeth knocked out.
related_events: Rayette coos over infant while seated on adjacent chair
Rayette draws attention to infant's cuteness
Bobby hands beer to Rayette upon request
Elton smiles gap-toothed at Bobby and suggests he get a child
Bobby stands up and stretches while responding to Elton's comment

name: Bobby Finds Rayette in Bed
description: Bobby enters the apartment and sees a rumpled blanket on the couch, a can of beer, and a cigarette burning in an ashtray on the coffee table. He calls out, 'Hello?!' and walks down the hall toward the bedroom. Standing in the doorway, he asks Rayette if she is sick, but she doesn't respond. He tells her he heard about Elton, and when she turns her gaze to the window, he says he understands her point.
related_events: Bobby notices rumpled blanket, beer can, and burning cigarette in the living room
Bobby calls out to Rayette and walks toward the bedroom
Bobby questions Rayette about her condition and Elton's news

name: Bobby Packs His Suitcase While Rayette Stays Silent
description: Bobby stands in the bedroom doorway, watching Rayette lie in bed with her back against the pillows, staring at the wall. He asks if she is sick, but she doesn’t respond. When he mentions Elton, she turns her gaze to the window. Bobby walks to the closet, takes out a suitcase, and begins packing clothes from the rack and dresser. He says his father is sick and he has to go home for two or three weeks. Rayette turns onto her side, making a snorting sound. Bobby closes the suitcase, sets it on the bed, and looks down at her. Her shoulders tremble as she weeps silently. He calls her 'DiPesto' and says he never promised anything would come of their relationship. He tells her he’ll send money and try to call. He says goodbye. She lets out a sob as he picks up the suitcase and leaves the room, walking down the hall.
related_events: Rayette ignores Bobby and turns her gaze to the window
Bobby acknowledges Rayette's silent protest and begins packing

name: Bobby Packs His Suitcase and Says Goodbye
description: Bobby stands in the bedroom and says he has to go home because his father is sick. He says he’ll be gone for two or three weeks. Rayette turns onto her side and lets out a snort of disbelief. Bobby goes to the closet, picks up a suitcase from the floor, and takes some clothes from the rack. He sets the suitcase on a chair and begins packing. He walks to the dresser, pulls out his underwear, and adds it to the suitcase. After closing and securing it, he lifts the suitcase, moves around the bed, and pauses to set it down on the mattress. He looks at Rayette, who remains turned away, her shoulders trembling. He calls her 'DiPesto' and says he never promised anything would come of their situation. He tells her he’ll send money and try to call from home. He says, 'Bye, Ray,' and as an audible sob escapes her, he picks up the suitcase and walks out of the room, heading down the hall.
related_events: Bobby announces he is leaving due to his father's illness
Bobby packs clothes and personal items into a suitcase
Rayette expresses disbelief with a snorting sound

name: Bobby Says Goodbye to a Weeping Rayette
description: Bobby closes the suitcase and sets it on the bed. He looks down at Rayette, who lies facing away, her shoulders trembling as she weeps silently. He speaks to her, his voice heavy with emotion, reminding her he never promised anything would come of their relationship. He tells her he’ll send money and call from where he’s going. After a pause, he says, 'Bye, Ray.' A sob escapes her. Without another word, Bobby picks up the suitcase and walks out of the bedroom, moving down the hall.
related_events: Bobby stops to look at Rayette as she weeps silently
Bobby promises to send money and call Rayette from away
Bobby says final goodbye to Rayette

name: Bobby Leaves and Rayette Weeps
description: Bobby closes the suitcase, fastens it, and picks it up. He moves around the bed toward the door, stops to set the suitcase on the bed, and looks down at Rayette, who remains turned away, her shoulders trembling silently. He tells her goodbye. As he picks up the suitcase and walks out of the bedroom and down the hall, an audible sob escapes Rayette.
related_events: Bobby closes and secures the suitcase before leaving the bedroom
Bobby picks up suitcase and exits the bedroom down the hall
Rayette lets out an audible sob as Bobby leaves

name: Bobby Intervenes at the Wrecked Car
description: Bobby pulls off onto the right-hand shoulder, stops the car, and gets out. He walks toward the center line, looking across the road. There, a long-haired young woman in Levi's and a parka is shoving her short-haired friend against the side of a damaged car, shouting something unclear. Bobby calls out, 'Hey! What's going on, what's the trouble?!' The woman turns, flips him off, and walks toward him, gesturing back at the wreck.
related_events: Bobby pulls car onto shoulder and stops
Bobby exits the car and moves to center line
Bobby shouts inquiry about the disturbance

name: Palm confronts Bobby after car breakdown
description: Bobby pulls off onto the shoulder and gets out, moving toward the center line as a long-haired young woman in a parka, Palm, turns from arguing with her friend Terry by the car. She flips Bobby off and strides over, gesturing angrily at the damaged vehicle behind her. 'Look at my car! Piece of shit!' she shouts. 'I just bought it brand new from a used-car lot, and the steering goes to the pot on me!' She curses the seller, vowing to punch the dealer, then calls to Terry to grab their things, announcing they’ve got a ride.
related_events: Palm responds with offensive gesture
Palm gestures angrily toward wreck while approaching Bobby
Palm complains about car malfunction to Bobby

name: Palm Demands Justice and Takes a Ride
description: Palm stands by the wrecked car, furious, shouting about losing seven hundred dollars on a vehicle she just bought from a used-car lot. She blames the seller, cursing him and threatening to go back and punch him. Bobby approaches and tells her she’s lucky no one was hurt. Ignoring his comment, Palm turns to him and asks for a ride. Without waiting for an answer, she calls out to Terry, telling her they’ve got a ride, and moves back to help gather their belongings from the roadside.
related_events: Palm demands compensation and threatens seller
Palm asks Bobby for a ride without waiting for reply
Palm signals Terry to join for the ride

name: Bobby and Rayette React to the Roadside Confrontation
description: Bobby stops his car on the shoulder and gets out, walking toward the center line as a long-haired young woman in a parka argues with her friend beside a damaged vehicle. He calls out, 'Hey! What's going on, what's the trouble?!' The woman flips him off and tells him to rotate. Inside Bobby's car, Rayette leans out the driver's window and asks, 'What'd she say?' The woman, ignoring them, gestures angrily at her wrecked car and shouts about losing seven hundred dollars on a faulty vehicle she bought from a used-car lot. She yells that she wants to punch the seller and demands a ride. Without waiting, she walks back to her friend, who is gathering their belongings from the road, and says, 'Come on, Terry, we got a ride!' Rayette watches the exchange and mutters, 'Jesus, what a rude person...'
related_events: Bobby responds with concern about safety
Rayette leans out window to ask for clarification
Rayette comments on Palm's rudeness

name: Terry Retrieves Belongings After Palm's Confrontation
description: Palm pushes Terry against the side of the car, accusing them in a heated moment. Afterward, Terry moves to the edge of the highway and begins picking up their belongings scattered on the road. Palm, having spoken to Bobby and Rayette, calls out for Terry to hurry, then walks back toward them as they collect their things.
related_events: Palm confronts Terry by pushing against car
Terry retrieves belongings from highway

name: Bobby Returns to the Car and Coaxes Rayette with a Nickname
description: After walking away, Bobby stops, turns back, and returns to the car. He leans down to the passenger window again and calls Rayette 'DiPesto.' He urges her to come along to Elton's, saying they can still have a good time. Rayette tells him he’s the pathetic one, not her. Bobby insists he’s going to Elton’s but stays by the car. He opens the door, gets inside, and puts his arm around her.
related_events: Bobby insults Rayette's appearance and demeanor
Bobby uses nickname 'DiPesto' to coax Rayette
Bobby attempts to persuade Rayette to go to Elton's

name: Rayette Confronts Bobby About His Treatment
description: Rayette sits in Bobby's car, refusing to go with him to Elton's. When he walks away, he returns and opens the car door, getting inside. He puts his arm around her and tries to reassure her, saying their friends know how he feels and that they would see her as the better person in the situation. Rayette tells him he treats her like a piece of crap and that he acts disrespectfully in front of Elton and Stoney. She says he should go ahead and leave her, that one day he might find her dead. Bobby hushes her, kisses her, and says he isn't going to leave. He urges her to come over to Elton's with him. She asks if he loves her. He hesitates, then replies, 'Well now, what do you think?' She pulls him into her arms.

Bobby reassures Rayette about others' perceptions of their relationship
Rayette threatens self-harm if Bobby abandons her

name: Bobby Comforts Rayette in the Car
description: Rayette sits in the passenger seat of Bobby's car, staring out through the windshield. Bobby walks away but stops, turns back, and returns to the car. He opens the door and gets inside, putting his arm around her. He kisses her and says, "Sssh, come on now... Be a good girl." She tells him he’ll find her dead one day, and he replies that he’s not going to leave her, kissing her again. He then invites her to go over to Elton’s. She asks if he loves her. He hesitates, then says, "Well now, what do you think?" She reaches over and pulls him into her arms.

Bobby reaffirms his commitment to stay with Rayette
Bobby invites Rayette to join the gathering at Elton's

Bobby gives an evasive but emotionally sufficient answer to Rayette's love inquiry

name: Bobby Invites Rayette to Elton's After Reconciliation
description: After a tense exchange, Bobby opens the car door and gets inside. He puts his arm around Rayette and kisses her, calming her. He suggests they go to Elton's to have a good time. Rayette asks if he loves her. Bobby hesitates, then replies, 'Well now, what do you think?' She pulls him into her arms, and they embrace.

name: Bobby Watches Tita Play Piano
description: Bobby arrives at the recording studio and stands behind the glass partition, watching Tita at the piano. She plays a piece by Bach, hunched over the keyboard, humming a long, monochromatic note that clashes with the music. Her unruly hair is pinned back, her glasses resting on the bench beside her. Two recording engineers glance at Bobby without interest and turn back to adjusting their dials and controls. One of them speaks into the microphone, calling out to Tita. She doesn’t respond at first, still playing. He calls her name again, more firmly. Annoyed, she stops and asks what they want. The engineer reminds her that her singing is not needed. She apologizes, saying she didn’t realize she was doing it again. He tells her they can take a break. She drops her head into her hands, saying she doesn’t want a break. The engineer asks what she’d like in her coffee. She mumbles without lifting her head, 'Tea.' Bobby asks the engineer to tell her he’s there. The engineer relays the message. Tita lifts her head, squints toward the booth, picks up her glasses, and puts them on.
related_events: Recording engineers ignore Bobby and focus on equipment
Bobby observes Tita playing piano through glass partition
Tita plays piano while humming discordant tones

name: Engineers Mock Tita's Singing During Recording
description: Two recording engineers watch Tita Dupea through the glass as she plays Bach on the piano, vocalizing in discordant tones. The first engineer remarks, 'There she goes again.' The second adds, 'My 1-year-old can carry a tune better than that.' Bobby starts to respond, but the second engineer flips a switch and speaks into the microphone, calling, 'Miss Dupea.' She doesn't answer at first, still playing. He calls again, more firmly, and she finally responds, annoyed. 'Yes.' He reminds her the session isn't for opera or musical comedy. She apologizes, asking if she was singing again. He replies sarcastically, 'If you want to call it that.' She says he should just tell her when she does it, and he says he is telling her—again. She complains that he waits until she's halfway through the movement, which tires her. He suggests a break. She drops her head into her hands, resting her elbows on the piano. The first engineer asks if she's going to cry. She says she doesn't want a break. The second engineer asks what she wants in her coffee. She mumbles without lifting her head, 'Tea.' Bobby asks them to tell her he's there. The engineer relays the message. She lifts her head, squints toward the booth, picks up her glasses from the bench, and puts them on.
related_events: First engineer comments on Tita's vocalizing
Second engineer criticizes Tita's singing ability

name: Engineer Calls Tita Over Intercom
description: The second engineer flips a toggle switch and speaks into the microphone, addressing Tita in the studio. 'Miss Dupea.' There is no response. She continues playing the piano, hunched over the keyboard, humming a long note. The engineer calls again, more emphatically. 'Miss Dupea.' Tita pauses, looks up, and replies with annoyance. 'Yes.'
related_events: Second engineer attempts to communicate with Tita via intercom
Tita continues playing without responding to intercom

name: Tita Resists Break and Rests Head on Piano
description: The second engineer suggests taking a break. Tita responds with annoyance, saying she does not want to take a break and that it is tiring to be interrupted halfway through the movement. She puts her elbows on the piano and drops her head into her hands. The first engineer asks if she is going to cry again. Tita lifts her head only after being told that Bobby is present.
related_events: Second engineer suggests taking a break during recording session
Tita expresses fatigue and reluctance toward taking a break
Tita rests her head on piano in visible frustration

name: Engineer Questions Tita's Emotional State During Recording
description: The first engineer asks if Tita is going to cry again, as she rests her head on the piano with her elbows propped up. She lifts her head, still wearing a strained expression, and says she doesn’t want to take a break. The second engineer asks what she would like in her coffee, and she mumbles a response without looking up. After a moment, she says she wants tea.
related_events: First engineer questions if Tita is about to cry

name: Bobby Arrives and Tita Recognizes Him
description: Bobby starts to respond to the engineers' remarks about Tita but stops himself. Instead, he asks the second engineer to tell Tita that he is there. The engineer speaks into the intercom, saying, "Miss Dupea, Bobby's here." Tita, who had been resting her head on her arms, lifts it and squints toward the booth. She reaches for her glasses on the piano bench, puts them on, and looks in his direction.

name: Bobby Confronts Elton After Personal Revelation
description: Elton sits on the rig floor opposite Bobby, who eats a sandwich. Elton suggests that a woman they know is in a difficult situation and says she confided in him, appearing troubled by her distress. He tries to normalize the situation, recalling how he reacted when someone once told him similar news. Bobby scowls, refusing to engage. Elton presses on, confirming the woman told him directly and that she is deeply upset. Bobby throws his sandwich onto the rig floor near Elton’s leg and empties his coffee cup before screwing it onto his thermos. He accuses Elton of presuming to compare their lives, calling the conversation ridiculous and saying it makes him want to vomit. Elton wipes mayonnaise off his pants and retorts that while Bobby may think himself better, he has no right to abandon someone in need. Bobby snaps back that he’s tired of Elton’s talk and grabs his jacket and lunch bucket. He jumps down from the rig and walks toward his car parked by the Field Office. Elton stands and hurls his hard hat in Bobby’s direction, shouting after him. As Bobby reaches his car, he calls out to the driller, Longcipher, who is leaning into a car with two men inside. Bobby announces he’s quitting. The driller gestures to the driver, then turns toward the office. Bobby repeats his announcement, demanding to be heard. The driller turns, says he doesn’t care, calls Bobby more trouble than he’s worth, and adds he’s glad to lose both of them. He goes inside and shuts the door. Bobby throws his belongings into the car. As he starts to get in, he pauses and looks back toward the rig.
related_events: Elton reveals personal news about a woman to Bobby
Bobby reacts angrily to Elton's comparison of their life experiences
Bobby throws his sandwich at Elton and spills coffee
Elton defends his perspective on responsibility and abandonment

name: Bobby Quits the Rig After Fight with Elton
description: After a heated argument with Elton, Bobby throws his sandwich on the rig floor and pours out the rest of his coffee. He grabs his jacket and lunch bucket, then jumps down and walks toward his car parked near the Field Office. Elton wipes mayonnaise from his pants and calls after him, but Bobby ignores him. As Bobby approaches his car, he calls out to the driller, Longcipher, telling him he's quitting. The driller gives directions to two men in a car, then turns and tells Bobby he doesn't care what he does, calling him and Elton both trouble. Bobby throws his things into his car. As he starts to get in, Elton stands up and hurls his hard hat in Bobby's direction.

Elton throws his hard hat toward Bobby after being insulted

name: Bobby Quits and the Driller Responds
description: As Bobby approaches his car, he calls out to the driller, shouting that he's quitting. The driller is bent down speaking to two men in a car parked near the Field Office. After gesturing for the driver to leave, the driller turns and walks toward the office. Bobby calls after him again, demanding to be heard. The driller stops, turns back, and tells Bobby he doesn't care what he does, calling him more trouble than he's worth and saying he's glad to be rid of him. Without another word, the driller goes inside and shuts the door. Bobby stands by his car, then throws his jacket and lunch bucket into it before starting to get in.

name: Bobby Intervenes in Elton's Arrest
description: Bobby, walking toward his car, notices two men confronting Elton on the rig platform. He sees Elton break free and run, only to be tackled and overpowered. As the men begin cuffing him, Bobby rushes back, shouting, and lunges at the first man to stop them. Elton yells at Bobby, warning him the men are law enforcement, but Bobby ignores the warning and attacks. The first man breaks free from Elton, grabs Bobby from behind, and slams him to the ground. He pins Bobby and raises a fist, preparing to handcuff him. Elton pleads with the men to leave Bobby alone, muttering that Bobby didn’t know who they were. Dazed, Bobby lifts his head and looks toward Elton. The second man steps forward, orders the first to release Bobby, and then shoves Elton toward their car.

name: Elton's Arrest and Final Request
description: Bobby sits up and demands to know what is happening. Elton tells him he was accused of robbing a filling station in the Indian Nation and had jumped bail, saying the two men are law enforcement who have finally caught up with him. The second man cuts Elton off and pushes him toward the car. As they force him into the back seat, Elton calls out to Bobby, saying they caught him a year later than expected and asking Bobby to tell Stoney to come get him. The car drives away with Elton inside. Bobby watches it until it disappears down the road, then leans against a pump casing, standing in silence.

name: Rayette Tries to Connect Through Music
description: Rayette, still in her waitress uniform, places a bowl of beer nuts on the coffee table and leans down to kiss Bobby, who sits on the couch with a can of beer. When he doesn’t respond, she kisses him more insistently, moving from his lips to his neck. He takes a drink without returning the affection. After the song ends, she says she wants to play it again. Bobby stops her, holding her hand. She suggests playing the other side instead, but he refuses and pulls her down onto the couch. She tells him to let her sing the song she picked. As she begins—'When there's a fire in your heart/Break the glass/Sound the alarm'—he picks up a pillow and holds it over his ear. Annoyed, she yanks the pillow away and snaps at him. He remains silent. She grabs the empty beer can he holds out and storms toward the kitchen, muttering that she’d do anything for him. She returns with a fresh beer, hands it to him, and sits back down, saying he’s too selfish to listen, even though all she wants is for him to pay attention to her singing. He looks at her name tag and tells her to take it off, then suggests they go out.

description: After Bobby refuses to let her play another song, Rayette sits up and looks away, hurt by his dismissal. She tells him how much she loves him, saying she started living the day she found him and would do anything for him. She asks why he won’t listen to her sing, pointing out that he and his whole family can play music, yet he won’t give her a moment of attention. As she speaks, her voice carries frustration and longing, pleading with him to show interest in what matters to her.

name: Bobby and Rayette's Argument Over a Beer
description: Bobby finishes his beer and holds the empty can out to Rayette, saying 'Cerveza.' She snatches the can from him, snaps 'Serveza yourself!' and stands up. As she turns toward the kitchen, Bobby says, 'But you heal fast.' From the kitchen, Rayette opens the refrigerator, takes out a new can, and returns. She hands the beer to him and sits back down. 'You can play the piano, an' your whole damn family can play on some type a musical instrument. An' all I'm askin' is for you to listen to my singing for one single little second,' she says. 'But you think you would? No, you're too damn selfish.' Earlier, after she had threatened to cut off his water, Bobby had responded, 'I'm too moved by your gentility to speak.'

description: Bobby enters the studio and opens his arms. Tita rushes into his embrace, burying her face in his shoulder. She begins to cry, and Bobby stands behind her, gently patting her back. A young man approaches, hands Bobby a paper cup of tea, and leaves. Bobby sets the cup on the piano, but Tita quickly picks it up and places it on the floor, explaining that the piano is a valuable old instrument once owned by Waldnit von Schnechter. She caresses the piano and watches as Bobby plays a brief flourish on the keys. They sit together on the bench as she continues to cry and search for tissues in her purse.

She tells Bobby it is a rare CB model that once belonged to Waldnit von Schnechter before the war. Bobby listens and then sits beside her. The injury has made it nearly impossible for him to hold a violin properly, ending his career as a fiddler. Bobby laughs at the story, saying Carl 'totaled his neck,' and shakes his head, still processing the news.

Tita urges him to visit his father, saying it’s the right thing to do. She asks him to go with her that night. Bobby hesitates, then refuses. Tita looks at him, visibly disappointed.

She turns toward the booth and calls out, 'Just a minute, please!' Then she looks back at Bobby, asking again if he thinks it's right that he should see his father. Tita insists on walking out with him, despite the second engineer calling out about her break time. She admits she’s not well-liked at work but says she needs to talk to Bobby about things that haven’t been settled. They move toward the exit, speaking quietly. Bobby suddenly decides to end the conversation, cuts it short, kisses her, and turns away. He walks down the stairs and leaves. Tita stands alone, struggling to hold back tears as she watches him go.

Stoney, Elton's wife, sits beside Rayette on the horseshoe banquette. Bobby's gesture draws no immediate response as Elton, missing his two front teeth, calls out in an Okie accent, 'Your ball, Ray.'

It veers to the right and knocks down only one pin. As she prepares for her second throw, Bobby calls out, telling her not to loft the ball and to release it as he had shown her. She bowls again, sending the ball down the right-hand gutter, then returns to the banquette and says the ball is too heavy. Bobby insists it’s not the ball. Stoney, seated nearby, steps up and bowls a strike.

name: Rayette's Gutter Ball and Bobby's Frustration
description: Rayette asks if it’s her turn again. Bobby tells her to go ahead and show some better form this time. She picks up the ball, steps forward, and throws it down the lane, but it veers into the right gutter. As she walks back, she says the ball keeps going wobbly on her. Bobby snaps, telling her to do exactly what he told her. Rayette looks to Elton, insisting she followed the instructions, but Bobby says she still has another ball coming. She returns to the rack, steps carefully down the lane, and releases the ball. It rolls slowly down the center, hits the pocket just right, and knocks down all the pins.

name: Rayette's Strike and Bobby's Rejection
description: Rayette picks up another ball from the rack, steps carefully to the lane, and releases it down the center. The ball rolls true, hits the pocket cleanly, and knocks down all the pins. Elton calls out, 'Atta boy, Ray!' Rayette returns to the banquette, sits beside Bobby, and looks at him expectantly. 'That was damn good, wad'n it? I finally did it,' she says. Bobby replies, 'Yeah, great,' without looking at her, then begins unlacing his bowling shoes. 'Why don't you throw Z's for frames, and then roll a strike on the last ball in the last frame of a losing game? Just wonderful.' He turns toward the adjacent lane where Twinky and Betty are setting up. 'Wasn't it, ladies?' Twinky points at herself and asks, 'Are you talking to us?' Rayette pulls off her rental shoes and throws them to the floor. 'I'm gonna go wait in the car.' Bobby leans back, arms stretched along the top of the banquette. 'Yeah, why don't you do that.' She grabs her sling-back and walks away.

name: Bobby Meets Betty and Twinky at the Bowling Alley
description: After Rayette leaves for the car, Bobby remains seated on the banquette, stretching his arms along the backrest. Two young women, Twinky and Betty, take over the adjacent lane. Twinky approaches and asks a question, drawing Bobby’s attention. Betty studies him closely and suddenly recognizes him as a television car salesman. She points to his wig, commenting on it. Bobby responds with a wry acknowledgment, confirming who he is in a tone that mixes irony and resignation. The two women exchange a look of knowing triumph. Twinky picks up a pencil and grabs the score sheet, writing down her number. She hands the sheet to Bobby and explains that she and Betty work together, offering companionship. Bobby glances at Betty and remarks on her potential usefulness. A waitress arrives to settle the tab, but Bobby stays in his seat, lost in thought as the moment settles around him.
